4.1 AVR Assembly, registers and the stack

The ATmega328P is an 8-bit AVR RISC device with general-purpose registers R0–R31. LDI accepts R16–R31. DDRD configures PORTD pin direction, PORTD sets output levels, and PINC reads digital input states. AVR subroutines are called with RCALL and return with RET; initialize the SRAM stack pointer before the first RCALL.
AVRASM2 project skeleton and stack initialization

At F_CPU = 16 MHz, one clock cycle is 1/16,000,000 s = 62.5 ns. One millisecond requires 16,000 cycles. In a countdown loop using SBIW (2 cycles) followed by BRNE (2 cycles when taken, 1 when not taken), N iterations consume exactly 4N − 1 cycles, excluding setup and subroutine overhead.

Example: A callable delay primitive with N = 3,997 uses 2 cycles to load R27:R26, 4N−1 = 15,987 cycles for the loop, 4 cycles for RET and 3 cycles for its RCALL, for 15,996 cycles in total. The enclosing DELAY_MS loop adds 4 cycles (SBIW and taken BRNE) per millisecond, giving 16,000 cycles for each normal iteration. The last iteration uses one fewer cycle, while its call/push/pop/return overhead adds a small fixed amount.

Thus the complete RCALL DELAY_MS operation has 16,000 × N_ms + 14 clock cycles (with N_ms from 1 to 65,535). For 500 ms the target is 8,000,000 cycles, so the routine gives 8,000,014 cycles ≈ 500.000875 ms, excluding instructions that switch the LED.
Reusable source file delay_ms.inc — place next to each .asm file
; File: delay_ms.inc (shared by all five experiments)
; Exact at 16 MHz: CALL + function = 16000*N + 14 cycles
; Clobbers: R26:R27 and flags. R24:R25 are restored.

The delay is a software busy-wait: its accuracy depends on the 16 MHz clock configuration, and it blocks other foreground work. For an advanced real-time implementation, use a hardware timer interrupt instead.
4.3 LED shift patterns and one-hot ring counter

For an eight-LED active-HIGH array attached to PD0–PD7, 0x01 lights LED0 and 0x80 lights LED7. LSL shifts a pattern toward more significant bits; LSR shifts toward less significant bits. Reset a one-hot pattern to 0x01 after the left shift yields zero, or to 0x80 after the right shift yields zero. Accumulating patterns use logical OR to add LEDs, and AND with an inverted mask to clear them one-by-one.

A common-cathode seven-segment unit has a common terminal connected to ground. With segment outputs on PD0–PD6 mapped to a, b, c, d, e, f, g (1 = ON), the byte for digit 0 is 0x3F. For A–F, appropriate segment patterns are stored as 16 bytes in Flash program memory. The AVR LPM instruction retrieves one byte via the Z pointer; in AVRASM2, multiply a program-memory table label by two to obtain its byte address.
If your physical display is common-anode, the polarities and common connection differ: do NOT use this wiring or code without adapting both. The five revised labs assume a COMMON-CATHODE digit.

7.1 Lab Work 1 — Designing Assembly Delay with One LED
Purpose: Calculate delay periods from CPU clock cycles, build a subroutine using an instruction-counted loop, and observe a single LED on PD0 switching ON and OFF at 1 Hz.
